Title: Official MtG iOS and Android apps.

Messages.Author: KzArashi
Messages.Body:
Source:  ICv2

"In what could be a gamechanger that could solidfy Magic sales for years to come, Wizards of the Coast today unveiled the Magic: The Gathering Toolbox, a free app for iOS devices that will be released later this month. An Android version of the app is in production and will come out soon thereafter. The new app supports the M:TG Trading Card Game (as well as Magic Online) with features that help players keep track of the points they earn with an advanced life counter for their Magic games, as well as aid in building decks, researching strategies, searching and filtering all 10,000 M:TG cards (it’s like having the Gatherer in your pocket). Other features include a schedule of events, player profile section, and both an “E-store” and a brick-and-mortar “Store Locator” function."

Well. No, I'm not a MtG player. But couldn't be só sad that VTES have not get his way to The next level, like his older brother.

I actually do think that "evolve or die" is good business advice. If we could only get the record companies to listen to it everyone would be better off...

On topic though.
Vampidroid is a great little app...for reference or settling quick disputes.
It's horrible for say designing a deck list or doing more advanced searches (Give me all followers of set in G3-4-5 that shares at least two disciplines with Lutz). Actually, from what I've seen we dont even have a tool on the computer that can do something like that.

I'd love to have an ipad app that is designed for deckbuilding. Giving me a very advances search interface, an easy way to run some basic statistics on the deck quickly, a quick way to post it on secretlibrary, cards with graphics (would be nice but might be a problem due to copyright)... And iPad would be the perfect platform for this since it is large enough to work with, the phones are just too small.

I work as a system developer and I would love to code an app like this. But that would require a database of all the cards (which maybe some nice person already has got somewhere), someone who knows the legal side to say something about how the copyright for the graphics works, and the main problem - an iOS developer license + a mac to develop this on (since iOS development is only officially supported on macs). And even though I would love to have such an application, I really cant find the motivation to spend that kind of money in order to make one myself.
